post.author: Tobias Lante
post.topic_summary: Factories should own all three layers of their industrial stack: data model, operational history, and decision logic. Most vendor contracts effectively let you keep only one.

comment_posted.comment_text:
The three-layer problem starts below the data model. Most commercial edge gateways ship with proprietary firmware that publishes to the vendor's cloud in a vendor-defined schema. The factory never sees raw signal data, only what the platform chose to surface. Owning the data model means nothing if the telemetry source is already locked to a vendor stack.

The open-protocol path (MQTT with SparkplugB or MTConnect at the edge, on hardware you control) is what makes the three-layer ownership actually achievable. If the edge device publishes to a broker you own, the raw timeseries is yours before any platform touches it. That is the foundation the data model, history, and decision logic all sit on.
